name: Conch Shell
lede: Conch Shell is a strong yellowish pink named for the inside of a conch's shell, first recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1925.

sections.title: Named for the shell's interior
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* records Conch Shell on plate 1 D 10, dating it to 1925, five years before their 1930 edition was published; our library cites it through that 1930 edition [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would place it in block 26, strong yellowish pink, 3.4 units from that block's centroid [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[meat]], [[grenadine-pink]], [[dark-salmon]] and [[dusty-salmon]], at 2.8, 3.2, 
The conch is a large sea snail whose shell shows a glossy, pink-orange interior once prized for cameos and trumpets, and the color names that lining rather than the shell's duller outer face [1]. It sits among the warm pinks near [[peach]] and [[coral]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Conch Shell covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 5 of them, as photographed [3]. The earliest is Correggio's *Salvator Mundi*, from about 1515 [3]. It is a vivid, saturated pink that rarely dominates enough of an aged, varnished canvas to register at our threshold, so its scarcity here reflects coverage, not absence from painters' palettes generally [3].
